source_text: Non tamen nos moveat aut turbet multorum nimia et abrupta perfidia, sed potius fidem nostram, praenuntiante rei veritate, corroboret. Ut quidam tales esse coeperunt, quia haec ante praedicta sunt, ita caeteri fratres ab ejusmodi caveant, quia et haec ante praedicta sunt, instruente Domino et dicente: Vos autem cavete, ecce praedixi vobis omnia. Vitate, quaeso vos, fratres, ejusmodi homines, et a latere atque auribus vestris perniciosa colloquia velut contagium mortis arcete, sicut scriptum est: Sepi aures tuas spinis, et noli audire linguam nequam. Et iterum: Corrumpunt ingenia bona confabulationes pessimae: Docet Dominus et admonet a talibus recedendum. Caeci sunt, inquit, duces caecorum. Caecus autem caecum ducens, simul in foveam cadunt. Aversandus est talis atque fugiendus quisquis fuerit ab Ecclesia separatus. Perversus est hujusmodi et peccat, et est a semetipso damnatus. An esse sibi cum Christo videtur qui adversus sacerdotes Christi facit, qui se a cleri ejus et plebis societate secernit? Arma ille contra Ecclesiam portat, contra Dei dispositionem repugnat. Hostis altaris, adversus sacrificium Christi rebellis, pro fide perfidus, pro religione sacrilegus, inobsequens servus, filius impius, frater inimicus, contemptis episcopis et Dei sacerdotibus derelictis, constituere audet aliud altare, precem alteram illicitis vocibus facere, Dominicae hostiae veritatem per falsa sacrificia profanare, nec scire quoniam qui contra ordinationem Dei nititur, ob temeritatis audaciam, divina animadversione punitur.
pass_a_gloss: Let not, however, the excessive and abrupt perfidy of many people move or disturb us, but rather let it strengthen our faith, with the truth of the matter having been foretold. The fact that certain individuals have begun to be such, because these things were predicted beforehand, let the other brothers beware of such people, because these things were also predicted beforehand, with the Lord instructing and saying: But you, beware, behold I have foretold all things to you. I ask you, brothers, to avoid such people and to keep pernicious conversations away from your side and ears, like a contagion of death, just as it is written: I have blocked my ears with thorns, and I will not hear the wicked tongue. And again: Bad conversations corrupt good minds: The Lord teaches and admonishes us to recede from such people. He says: Blind are the leaders of the blind. However, a blind person leading a blind person, they both fall into a pit together. Someone who has been separated from the Church must be shunned and avoided. Such a person is perverse and sins, and is condemned by their own self. Does someone who acts against the priests of Christ seem to be with Christ, who separates themselves from the association of Christ's clergy and people? That person bears arms against the Church, rebels against God's disposition. They are an enemy of the altar, a rebel against Christ's sacrifice, perfidious for the faith, sacrilegious for religion, a disobedient servant, an impious son, an enemy brother, having despised and abandoned the bishops and God's priests, they dare to establish another altar, to make another prayer with illicit voices, to profane the truth of the Lord's sacrifice through false sacrifices, and they do not know that whoever resists God's ordination is punished by divine retribution due to the audacity of their temerity.

pass_b_english: The excessive and abrupt perfidy of many must not move or disturb us; rather, with the truth of the matter already foretold, it should strengthen our faith. Because certain men have begun to be such as were predicted beforehand, the rest of the brothers must beware of such people, since these things were also foretold, with the Lord instructing and saying, "But you, beware; behold, I have foretold everything to you" (Mark 13:23). Brothers, I beg you, avoid such men and bar pernicious talk from your side and ears as if it were a contagion of death, just as it is written: "I have hedged my ears with thorns; I will not listen to a wicked tongue" (Sirach 28:28). And again: "Bad company corrupts good character" (1 Corinthians 15:33). The Lord teaches and admonishes us to withdraw from such people. He says, "They are blind guides of the blind" (Matthew 15:14), and, "If the blind lead the blind, both will fall into a pit" (Matthew 15:14). Anyone separated from the Church must be shunned and avoided. Such a person is perverse and sins, and stands self-condemned. Does he think he is with Christ who acts against Christ's priests and separates himself from the fellowship of Christ's clergy and people? He bears arms against the Church and rebels against God's ordinance. He is an enemy of the altar, a rebel against Christ's sacrifice, faithless in faith, sacrilegious in religion, a disobedient servant, an impious son, a hostile brother. Having despised and abandoned the bishops and God's priests, he dares to set up another altar, to offer another prayer with illicit voices, and to profane the truth of the Lord's sacrifice through false sacrifices. He does not realize that whoever resists God's ordination is punished by divine retribution because of the audacity of his temerity.

Pass A and B are consistent with the source.
